meta.title: The Rain Chant
meta.textType: story: a chant with repeated lines

paragraphs: It rains all day, and Teacher Kim's class is in the classroom. The rain is loud on the roof. The children look at the gray sky. Mia wears a red coat, and Leo has blue boots. May has a yellow hat, and Lily wears a green sweater. "Oh dear," says Mia. "The weather is bad." "Let's make a rain chant," says Teacher Kim. "What do we say?" asks Leo. Teacher Kim writes on the board: "Bad, bad, bad weather!"

The class says it again and again. "Bad, bad, bad weather!" "Worse, worse, worse weather!" "The worst weather in the jungle!" Leo adds a fat frog and a star behind the cloud. "A fat frog in the wild rain!" says May. The frog is big, and the star is small. Rain falls in the swimming pool, too. "Rain in the swimming pool!" says Mia. The chant is loud, and Lily and May laugh.

Lily puts up her hand. "The end must be better," she says. "Better, better, better weather!" "A rainbow in the sky!" The class says it again, loud and happy. It is a lot of fun. Then the rain stops, and the sun comes out. "Look at the window!" says May. The children run to the window with their umbrellas. Why do they need umbrellas now? No one knows, and Teacher Kim laughs. There is a big rainbow in the sky behind the playground!
text.summary: It rains all day, so Teacher Kim's class makes a rain chant. The chant gets worse and worse, and then Lily asks for a better end.
